sections.text: The Power of Coding Coding powers every corner of our digital world. sections.heading: Hi! From The Founders
sections.text: Having grown up in a society where there is endless talent but opportunities having been unequally distributed, we created Zaio to democratize access to these opportunities. At the core of our organisation, we believe that if this untapped talent is given just a chance at unlocking its potential, the world in which we will live in will be even better than it is today. We believe so much in realizing this world one day that we gave ourselves a constant reminder in our name; Zaio! "Zaio is adapted from the Nguni word ‘Okuzayo’ which means the future." We met on a university campus and although we came from different areas of the African continent, namely Kenya, Malawi and South Africa, we were brought together through a shared vision; to cultivate leaders that will drive the future of continental and global innovation. We want to share this vision with the world. As we have evolved as individuals and as a company, we have remained true to this. It is our mission to help others reach their full potential through education and help organisations get the best out of their people. Collectively, we can create the future we want to live in. - Founders of Zaio. Mvelo Hlophe CEO Asif Hassam Upskilling Lead Harjot Singh CMO Akhil Boddu COO

sections.heading: What is an Occupational Certificate?
sections.text: A nationally-recognised, work-focused qualification that sits between a short course and a full degree. A degree is longer and more theoretical (3–4 years); a higher certificate is quick but limited. An OC with Zaio is the middle path: QCTO-accredited, ~1.5 years, built around real workplace modules and projects for direct entry into a job.

sections.heading: Do I need coding experience to apply?
sections.text: No. Our Occupational Certificates are designed for beginners. The only entry requirement is an NQF Level 4 qualification (a Matric certificate or equivalent), and we take you from the fundamentals to job-ready.

sections.heading: Is the qualification accredited?
sections.text: Yes. Zaio Institute of Technology is accredited and quality-assured by the Quality Council for Trades and Occupations (QCTO), Accreditation No. 07-QCTO/SDP220925101328. Each certificate is a nationally-recognised NQF Level 5 qualification.

sections.heading: How long does it take?
sections.text: About 1.5 years. That combines knowledge modules, practical skills and formal workplace experience, ending in an external assessment through the QCTO. Much faster than a 3–4 year degree.

sections.heading: How do I learn: online or in person?
sections.text: Online and live. You learn from anywhere in South Africa with live sessions and support, while completing practical and workplace modules built into the qualification.

sections.heading: Are there funded or payment options?
sections.text: Yes. Funded options are available and we offer flexible payment plans. Speak to an advisor when you apply and we'll help you find the right option for your situation.

sections.heading: Investing in Skills Development
sections.text: For Large Companies (with turnovers exceeding R50 million) and Qualifying Small Enterprises (QSEs), Skills Development is a paramount element on the BEE Scorecard, contributing up to 25 points out of 100. The Skills Development Scorecard encompasses a dedicated Learnership category, available to both employees and unemployed BEE candidates, making accredited Learnerships through the Zaio Programme the most efficient means of accumulating BEE Skills Development points. This is primarily because, through a Learnership, your company can claim the training expenses (and, in certain cases, provide stipends to learners) while actively participating in the accredited Learnership Programme. It's crucial to recognize that Economic Active Population (EAP) targets are applicable to the Skills Development Scorecard. In this context, Zaio excels, boasting diversity statistics well above industry averages.

sections.heading: How Does It Operate?
sections.text: The Skills Development Scorecard evaluates monetary expenditure on black candidates and the number of black individuals enrolled in Learnerships and structured work-based learning programs. In essence, it emphasizes achieving targets related to (i) training expenses (in relation to total payroll) and (ii) headcount (in relation to total staff count) for those undergoing training. Additionally, note that certain sector scorecards necessitate ICT skills training to qualify, a requirement seamlessly met by the Zaio Programmes.

sections.heading: Total Payroll
sections.text: Large Companies are mandated to allocate 6% of their total payroll for the training of BEE Candidates, while QSEs are required to allocate 3% of their total payroll. This allocation earns 8 points on the BEE scorecard. Furthermore, an additional 4 points can be earned by training Black disabled employees.

sections.heading: Headcount Requirement
sections.text: The headcount requirement entails 2.5% of your total staff, rounded up to the nearest integer. For example, if you employ up to 40 staff, you would require 1 learner. In the case of a staff complement of 400, 10 learnerships would be needed, and so forth. By enrolling the appropriate number of candidates in a Learnership, you can earn 8 points.

sections.heading: Bonus Points for Employment
sections.text: An additional 5 points can be garnered if Zaio Learners are employed at the conclusion of their Learnership. This employment can be on a fixed-term contract or a permanent basis. It's noteworthy that the Learner does not need to be employed by your company; if the Learner secures employment with another company, you can still obtain the bonus points. Zaio programmes offer interview preparation and job readiness training to ensure the candidates land a job.

Participating entities can potentially ascend by 1 or 2 BEE recognition levels by meeting minimum requirements. To qualify, the entity must: Meet the 40% sub-minimums for each priority element (ownership, skills development, preferential procurement, supplier development, and enterprise development), or achieve an average of 50% (if a generic company) across the three priority elements, or an average of 0% (if a QSE) in two of the three priority elements, including ownership. Improve its BEE score annually. Achieve a full score on the Skills Development Scorecard (if a generic). Provide 12-month full-time employment contracts (ideally suited to Zaio learnerships) to a number of Black youth (aged 18 – 35 years) as determined by the higher of: 1.5% of last year's headcount. 1.5% of average NPAT (net profit after tax) over the last 3 years, converted to headcount by dividing by R55,000. A target set in a table based on annual revenue or headcount. To advance by 1 BEE level, the YES company must meet the target and achieve 2.5% permanent employment. To ascend by 2 BEE levels, the YES company must meet double the target and achieve 5% permanent employment. In certain circumstances, an additional 3 points can also be earned, potentially propelling the company to yet another level.

sections.heading: What happens if I fail the interview and do not get the job?
sections.text: Due to the competitive nature of hiring for cloud roles, we do not guarantee placement, there are many mitigating circumstances. What we will do is provide you with the support, skills, and certifications to be best prepared for the interview.

sections.heading: Will I receive a certificate at the end of the bootcamp?

sections.heading: What makes this Cloud & DevOps Engineer course different from other cloud programs?
sections.text: Most cloud bootcamps teach AWS services in isolation, you leave able to click through the console but unable to build the applications you're supposed to deploy. You graduate understanding every layer of the stack, not just the top one, and prepared for both Cloud Engineer and DevOps Engineer job titles.

sections.heading: Do I need to know AWS before I start?

In fact, we deliberately spend the first four months on programming and application fundamentals before touching AWS, because you can't meaningfully deploy something to the cloud if you've never built or run it yourself.

sections.heading: Will I actually deploy real applications on AWS?
